intro: A change of employer on a Skilled Worker visa needs a new application with your new sponsor. We help you time it correctly, so your change of employer doesn’t put your status at risk.
cardText: Moving to a new job with a new sponsor.

checklist.item: A job offer from a licensed sponsor
A role that meets the skill and salary rules

purposesTitle: What changes when you move job

purposes.title: New salary rules
purposes.text: The new role must meet the rules that apply to you.

purposes.title: Timing
purposes.text: Get the new application in before you start.

notCovered: Starting the new job before applying
A new employer without a sponsor licence
A role that doesn’t meet the salary rules

rules.title: Apply before you start
rules.text: You must make a new application, with a new CoS, before you start the new job.

rules.title: Your old employer
rules.text: Your current sponsor reports when you leave. Plan your notice period around your application.

rules.title: Settlement
rules.text: Under the government’s plans, Skilled Workers earning £50,271 or more in 3 of the last 5 years keep a 5-year route to ILR. [Read about the ILR changes](/ilr-changes-2026/)

boxTitle: Want a second pair of eyes before you apply?
boxText: A consultation costs far less than a refused application. We’ll check your case against the current rules and tell you honestly where you stand.

sections.heading: How a Skilled Worker change of employer works
sections.text: Your new employer must hold a sponsor licence and assign you a Certificate of Sponsorship. You then make a new Skilled Worker application before you start the new job. If you’re only moving within the same employer to a different role, a change of employer application may not be needed, but some changes still need one.

faqs.q: Do I need a new visa for a change of employer?
faqs.a: Yes. You need a new Skilled Worker application with the new employer’s CoS.

faqs.q: Can I start my new job straight away?
faqs.a: Apply before you start the new job. We’ll advise on timing for your case.

faqs.q: Will a change of employer affect my settlement?
faqs.a: Time with different sponsors on the Skilled Worker route can usually count, as long as there are no gaps in your permission.
